review: 505.5-1: polarities inverted (a roll that misses the lights still performs 505.5's roll, while no Attraction is where the turn-based action does not happen); roll_misses_lights set to other, no_attraction to does_not_fire with a one-fact delta.

505.6b-3: decisions had A pass with an empty stack before B's verdict, contradicting cast_creature where Grizzly Bears is on the stack; decisions rewritten so B's verdict is recorded at B's first priority in both variants.

scenarios.title: The active player puts a lore counter on each Saga they control as the precombat main phase begins

setup.notes: The setup is the moment the precombat main phase begins, before its turn-based actions. History of Benalia (a Saga with chapter abilities) has 1 lore counter, so chapter I has already happened.

decisions: The first main phase begins: the turn-based action adds a lore counter to each Saga its active player controls; this does not use the stack.
If a chapter ability triggers, A puts it on the stack and both players pass priority so it resolves.
A passes priority with an empty stack; the main phase ends.

variants.label: own_saga_precombat
variants.expected: History of Benalia receives a second lore counter without using the stack; chapter II triggers, and when it resolves A controls one 2/2 white Knight creature token with vigilance.

variants.label: postcombat_main
variants.delta: The step is main2 (the postcombat main phase) instead of main1.
variants.expected: History of Benalia keeps 1 lore counter; no chapter ability triggers and A controls no Knight token.

variants.label: opponents_saga
variants.delta: History of Benalia is on B's battlefield instead of A's; A is still the active player.
variants.expected: History of Benalia keeps 1 lore counter; no chapter ability triggers and B controls no Knight token.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge adds the lore counter in PhaseHandler on entering MAIN1 with no stack object; the chapter trigger caused by the added counter is what reaches the stack.

scenarios.title: The active player rolls to visit their Attractions as the precombat main phase begins

setup.notes: The setup is the moment the precombat main phase begins, before its turn-based actions. Balloon Stand is the variant with lights 2 and 6. The visit roll is fixed to 6 in the base variant.

decisions: The first main phase begins: A rolls one six-sided die to visit their Attractions; this does not use the stack. The roll is 6.
Balloon Stand's visit ability triggers; A puts it on the stack and chooses the mode that creates a 1/1 Balloon token.
Both players pass priority; the visit ability resolves.

variants.label: roll_on_a_light
variants.expected: A rolls a 6, which matches a light of Balloon Stand, so Balloon Stand is visited; its ability resolves and A controls one 1/1 red Balloon creature token with flying.

variants.label: roll_misses_lights
variants.expected: A rolls a 4, which matches no light of Balloon Stand; Balloon Stand is not visited, its ability does not trigger and A controls no Balloon token.

variants.label: no_attraction
variants.delta: Balloon Stand is not on the battlefield, so A controls no Attraction.
variants.expected: A does not roll to visit Attractions; no die roll occurs and A controls no token.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge rolls in PhaseHandler on entering MAIN1 only if the active player controls an Attraction. The die result has to be fixed through a test hook; the lights of Balloon Stand (2 and 6 is Variant A) depend on the variant Forge picks when the card is created.

scenarios.title: Creature, sorcery and artifact spells can be cast only by the active player in a main phase

setup.notes: A holds one card of each kind. Each candidate is judged on its own with all four lands untapped. The stack is empty and A has priority.

decisions: A receives priority with an empty stack; the can_play verdict for each card in A's hand is recorded.

variants.label: main_phase
variants.expected: can_play is true for Grizzly Bears, Divination, Sol Ring and Lightning Bolt.

variants.label: combat_step
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: can_play is false for Grizzly Bears, Divination and Sol Ring; can_play is true for Lightning Bolt.

variants.label: nonactive_player
variants.delta: The hand and lands belong to B instead of A, and A is still the active player in main1; B receives priority after A passes with an empty stack.
variants.expected: can_play is false for Grizzly Bears, Divination and Sol Ring; can_play is true for Lightning Bolt.

scenarios.forge_notes: The nonactive_player variant moves the whole setup to B (B's battlefield and hand hold the lands and spells above).

scenarios.title: The active player may play a land from hand in a main phase only with an empty stack, priority, and no land played this turn

setup.notes: A has not played a land this turn. The stack is empty and A has priority.

decisions: A receives priority; the can_play verdict for the Forest in A's hand is recorded.

variants.label: land_already_played
variants.delta: A has already played a land this turn (the Mountain on the battlefield).
variants.expected: Playing Forest is not legal (can_play false).

variants.label: stack_not_empty
variants.delta: A's Lightning Bolt targeting B is on the stack (A tapped the Mountain for it) and A holds priority.
variants.expected: Playing Forest is not legal (can_play false).

variants.label: combat_step
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: Playing Forest is not legal (can_play false).

variants.label: nonactive_player
variants.delta: The Forest is in B's hand instead of A's; A is the active player in main1 and B receives priority after A passes with an empty stack.
variants.expected: Playing Forest is not legal for B (can_play false).

scenarios.forge_notes: The tapped Mountain was not played this turn in the base variant, so the played-land counter is 0 there; in land_already_played the counter is 1.

scenarios.title: An effect allowing additional lands makes a second land play legal

setup.notes: A has already played a land this turn (the Mountain). The stack is empty and A has priority.

decisions: A receives priority; the can_play verdict for the Forest in A's hand is recorded.

variants.label: no_extra_land_effect
variants.expected: Playing Forest is not legal (can_play false).

variants.label: with_exploration
variants.delta: A also controls Exploration on the battlefield.

scenarios.forge_notes: The played-land counter is 1 in both variants.

scenarios.title: Playing a land does not use the stack, so it cannot be responded to or countered

setup.notes: A has not played a land this turn. B has two untapped Islands.

decisions: A plays Forest from hand (in cast_creature: casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests); A then passes priority.
B receives priority; B's can_play and has_legal_target verdicts for Counterspell are recorded, and B passes.
In cast_creature, Grizzly Bears then resolves; in both variants A then passes with an empty stack, B passes, and the main phase ends.

variants.label: play_land
variants.expected: The Forest enters A's battlefield at once; no stack object exists, so Counterspell has no legal target (has_legal_target false, can_play false) and B has no response window.

variants.label: cast_creature
variants.delta: A casts Grizzly Bears (tapping both Forests) instead of playing the Forest.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is on the stack and B receives priority: Counterspell has a legal target (has_legal_target true, can_play true). B passes; Grizzly Bears resolves and enters A's battlefield.
